title: AES-GCM (Galois/Counter Mode)
summary: AES-GCM is an authenticated encryption mode. It combines AES-CTR (counter mode for encryption) with GHASH (Galois field multiplication for authentication). Output: ciphertext + authentication tag (128 bits). Used in TLS 1.3, IPsec, and most modern protocols. Nonce: 96 bits (recommended) or 128 bits. AAD (Additional Authenticated Data) is authenticated but not encrypted.

structure.meaning: Initialization vector. Must be unique per key (nonce reuse is catastrophic).
Counter for AES-CTR. Starts at 1 (0 reserved for GHASH). Increments for each block.
Plaintext XOR keystream (AES-CTR). Each block: AES(key, nonce || counter).
Galois field (GF(2^128)) multiplication. Authenticates ciphertext + AAD. Polynomial: x^128 + x^7 + x^2 + x + 1.
Authentication tag = GHASH(AAD, ciphertext, lengths) XOR AES(key, nonce || 0). Truncated to tag length.
Additional Authenticated Data. Authenticated but not encrypted (e.g., packet headers).

notes: AES-GCM is the most common AEAD mode (TLS 1.3, IPsec, SSH).
Nonce reuse is catastrophic: reveals XOR of plaintexts and allows forgery.
GHASH uses GF(2^128) multiplication (carryless multiply, available on modern CPUs).
AES-GCM is fast: ~1-2 GB/s on modern hardware (AES-NI + CLMUL).
Tag length: 128 bits (recommended), 96 bits (minimum for security).
